problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14060128/assets/0457cb819e6f39ef9c0978e356cff788e1cf5edbef9cbf844a054ab777b70eac.png)

The path ${C}_{1}$ consists of a the line segment from the point $A(-2,0)$ to the point $B(0,1),$ and the path ${C}_{2}$ consists of the line segment from the point $B(0,1)$ to the point $D(1,1).$

Given that ${\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r=-\frac{3}{2},$ evaluate ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=(x-2y)\,i+(y-x)\,j,$ and $C={C}_{1}\cup {C}_{2}.$
worked_solution:
We will use the fact that

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r.
$$

We're given the value of the second integral, so we only need to work out the first.

The path ${C}_{1}$ is the line segment from $A$ to $B.$  It can be parametrized as

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{1}(t) & =a+t(b-a) \\  & =⟨-2,0⟩+t(⟨0,1⟩-⟨-2,0⟩) \\  & =⟨-2+2t,t⟩ \\  & =(-2+2t)i+t\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $0<t<1.$ Along this segment, we have $x=-2+2t$ and $y=t.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F({r}_{1}(t)) & =(x-2y)\,i+(y-x)\,j \\  & =((-2+2t)-2t)\,i+(t-(-2+2t))\,j \\  & =-2\,i+(2-t)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the derivative, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{1}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2+2t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)j \\  & =2\,i+j\end{aligned}
$$

We can now compute the dot product:

$$
\begin{aligned}F({r}_{1}(t))\cdot {r}_{1}^{′}(t) & =(-2\,i+(2-t)\,j)\cdot (2\,i+j) \\  & =-2-t\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can evaluate the integral, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F({r}_{1}(t))\cdot {r}_{1}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t+(-\frac{3}{2}) \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(-2-t)\,\text{d}t-\frac{3}{2} \\  & ={[-2t-\frac{{t}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{1}-\frac{3}{2} \\  & =[-2(1)-\frac{{1}^{2}}{2}-0]-\frac{3}{2} \\  & =-\frac{5}{2}-\frac{3}{2} \\  & =-4\end{aligned}
$$
